title: Parmesan-Crusted Chicken with Garlic Green Beans
subtitle: juicy chicken cutlets under a crunchy golden Parmesan-panko crust, with garlicky buttered green beans and rice
imageAlt: Golden Parmesan-crusted chicken cutlets with buttered green beans and white rice on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Slice each breast in half through the side to make 2 thin cutlets; they cook evenly and fast.
Start the rice first; it's ready when the chicken is.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Cutlets
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Slice each breast in half through the side to make 4 cutlets and season with the salt, pepper and paprika.

steps.title: Crust
steps.text: Mix the panko, Parmesan, garlic powder and melted butter. Lay the cutlets on the sheet, spread the tops thinly with the mayonnaise and press the crumbs on firmly.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 18–20 minutes, until the crust is golden and the thickest part reads 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Green beans
steps.text: Meanwhile, boil the beans in salted water 4 minutes and drain. In the same pot, melt the butter over medium, cook the garlic 30 seconds, then toss the beans in it with the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest the chicken 3 minutes and serve with the rice and green beans.

fixIt.fix: Move the sheet up a rack and bake 2–3 minutes more, watching closely.
Pat the chicken dry before the mayonnaise, and press the crumbs on firmly.
Pull it at 74°C (165°F); thin cutlets overshoot quickly.

saleTip: Chicken breasts drop to about $9.90/kg in No Frills multi-packs; freeze them in pairs.
swap: Boneless thighs: bake 20–22 minutes to 74°C (165°F). Broccoli instead of beans: boil 3 minutes.
leftovers: Slice cold cutlets into wraps or onto a salad.
doneness: Chicken cutlets at 74°C (165°F) in the thickest part (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested Parmesan-crusted chicken methods (Hellmann's Canada, Canadian Living): a thin coat of mayonnaise under a Parmesan-panko crust, baked hot at 220°C.
prepAhead: Mix the crumb topping up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the fridge.
Trim the beans up to 2 days ahead.
reheat: Cutlets on a rack at 200°C (400°F) for 8–10 minutes, until 74°C (165°F); the crust stays crisp.

basic.note: Parmesan chicken with plain buttered beans and rice; no paprika or garlic.

stepNotes.4: Basic: skip the garlic; just butter and salt.

fancy.note: A lemon butter sauce spooned over the chicken.

addSteps.title: Lemon butter
addSteps.text: Melt the butter in a small pot over low with the garlic powder, then stir in the lemon zest and 2 tbsp juice. Spoon over the chicken at the table.

plating: Slice each cutlet on an angle and fan it over the rice.
Lemon butter spooned over just before serving.

why.0-4: A thin coat of mayonnaise glues the crumbs on and keeps the chicken juicy.
why.0-6: Parmesan browns and crisps in the oven, so the crust tastes like frico.
why.0-8: Buttered crumbs turn golden in the oven without frying.

funFact: Parmesan has to age at least 12 months before it can carry the name Parmigiano Reggiano.

keeps.note: freeze baked cutlets, not the beans
